name: run_diagnostics
description:
Start, poll, or stop a diagnostic -- the exact `name` from list_diagnostics, never invented. Only one diagnostic can be active at a time, and while one is running, EVERY other tool (not just run_diagnostics) is refused -- the customer effectively can't do anything else until it finishes, times out, or is stopped, so make sure they understand that when you start one.

- A diagnostic with long_running=false runs and returns its result immediately (status "completed") -- nothing is blocked afterward.
- A diagnostic with long_running=true starts in the background and returns immediately (status "started") -- it does NOT block waiting for the result. Tell the customer it's running, that no other request can be handled until it's done, and that they can ask you to check on it or stop it; do not imply it already finished.
- Calling run_diagnostics again with that SAME name checks on it: status "running" (still going, with elapsed_s), "completed"/"error" (with the result -- only returned once), or "timed_out".
- If the customer asks for anything else while one is running, you'll get an error naming the running diagnostic -- relay that to the customer and ask whether they want to stop it (call run_diagnostics with the stop diagnostic's exact name from list_diagnostics) or wait.
- The stop diagnostic always works regardless of what's running and stops whatever diagnostic is currently active.

function.description: The exact `name` of a diagnostic from list_diagnostics (including the stop diagnostic, to interrupt whatever's currently running).

candidate_devices.description: Optional list of devices/groups/scenes that seem relevant to this diagnostic, with relevance scores -- e.g. for a fuzzy request like "why is my master bathroom scene so intermittent", include every device/scene whose name matches "master bathroom". Does not change which diagnostic function runs; carried along as context for what the diagnostic concerns (echoed back in run_diagnostics' response) so it's clear which devices/scenes the customer meant, even though today's diagnostics are all system-wide, not per-device.

device_id.description: The unique device or group/scene identifier

score.description: Relevance score from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive (higher is better)

candidate_routines.description: Optional list of routines/folders that seem relevant to this diagnostic, with relevance scores -- same idea as candidate_devices but for routines/folders.

score.description: Relevance score from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive (higher is better)
